Cost note: Coris Bank International and Ecobank Burkina publish no non-resident opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee (web search budget exhausted in pass 2, so figures come from the existing min_deposit_fees text and were not re-verified against a bank tariff).

Documents required: Passport, Malian residence certificate and in-branch opening.
Minimum deposit & fees: Not published.
Banks accepting non-residents: None known for non-residents; BDM (Banque de Développement du Mali) and Ecobank Mali serve residents.
Restrictions: UEMOA exchange control (BCEAO instruction 09/07/2025/RFE on non-resident accounts effective August 2025); security crisis and travel warnings make in-person opening impractical.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Orange Money Mali or Moov Money with local SIM and ID; Wise does not support Mali payouts.
Cost note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so no opening fee, deposit or monthly fee applies.

Documents required: Passport with visa or residence card, proof of local accommodation or residence certificate, in-person KYC.
Minimum deposit & fees: not published
Banks accepting non-residents: none known for non-residents (Ecobank Guinee, BICIGUI, Orabank, AFG Bank serve residents).
Restrictions: Exchange controls on Guinean francs; branch visit and local residence documents expected.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Orange Money/MTN MoMo with local SIM.
Cost note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here, so all cost fields are null; local banks serve residents only.

Documents required: Passport, local address, residence or professional link to the country; requirements not published.
Minimum deposit & fees: Not published.
Banks accepting non-residents: None known for non-residents; local banks include Ecobank Guine-Bissau, Orabank, Banco da Uniao.
Restrictions: BCEAO/WAEMU exchange controls; 2026 non-resident CFA account rule covers only WAEMU citizens abroad; very low banking penetration.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Mobile money (Orange Money) once locally registered; Wise not available locally.
Cost note: Non-residents cannot realistically open a personal account here, so no cost figures apply (all null).

Documents required: Passport, proof of address, often residence proof, notarised or certified ID for non-resident applications; initial deposit.
Minimum deposit & fees: Monthly maintenance roughly XOF 1,000-6,000; opening deposit varies by bank, not published.
Banks accepting non-residents: Ecobank Senegal (possible non-resident opening with certified documents), CBAO Attijariwafa, Societe Generale Senegal, Bank of Africa Senegal.
Restrictions: BCEAO/UEMOA foreign-exchange regulation of non-resident accounts, XOF pegged to EUR, branch visit usually needed.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Wave and Orange Money mobile wallets (need local SIM/ID); Wise, Revolut.
Cost note: Monthly maintenance at Senegalese banks is roughly XOF 1,000-6,000 (lower bound about USD 1.80 at XOF 560/USD); opening fees and deposits at Ecobank Senegal are not published.

Documents required: Passport, proof of address, residence or work permit at most banks, Gambia TIN, and notarised ID for non-residents where accepted; branch visit required.
Minimum deposit & fees: not published (monthly maintenance reportedly around GMD 2-15).
Banks accepting non-residents: Ecobank Gambia reportedly considers non-residents with notarised ID, address proof and a Gambia TIN; Access Bank, GTBank and Trust Bank reportedly require residence/work permits or local ID.
Restrictions: No remote non-resident onboarding found; standard KYC expects local ID and in-person visit; small market with limited correspondent banking and USD access.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Wave and Afrimoney mobile money (local SIM needed); Western Union, MoneyGram and Wise transfers to GMD.
Cost note: Monthly maintenance at Gambian banks reportedly about GMD 2-15 (upper bound about USD 0.20 at GMD 72/USD), not from an Ecobank Gambia tariff; opening fee and minimum deposit are not published, so null.

Documents required: Passport, proof of address, photo, residence permit if applicable, TIN if available; branch visit with ID.
Minimum deposit & fees: Initial deposit varies by bank; not published.
Banks accepting non-residents: Rokel Commercial Bank and others require branch visit; Ecobank Sierra Leone policy not published.
Restrictions: Bank of Sierra Leone permits residents and non-residents to hold foreign-currency accounts, but banks rarely onboard non-residents remotely; AML de-risking.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Orange Money and Afrimoney need local SIM/ID; Wise/remittance services from abroad.
Cost note: Not published: Rokel Commercial Bank and others require a branch visit, and initial deposits and fees are not published.

Documents required: Passport, proof of address or residence, residence permit if applicable, TIN if available, passport photos, initial deposit; in-branch KYC.
Minimum deposit & fees: not published
Banks accepting non-residents: Ecobank Liberia, LBDI, Afriland First Bank, GT Bank Liberia; no bank confirmed to open personal accounts remotely for non-residents.
Restrictions: Dual USD/LRD economy; correspondent-banking de-risking; Central Bank of Liberia KYC rules; in-person presence usually required.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Orange Money or MTN Lonestar MoMo with local SIM; Western Union/MoneyGram for transfers.
Cost note: Ecobank Liberia, LBDI, Afriland and GT Bank Liberia do not publish non-resident personal account opening fees, minimum deposits or monthly fees, so all figures are null.

Documents required: Passport, residence permit or visa, local address proof and income justification; in-branch only.
Minimum deposit & fees: Not published.
Banks accepting non-residents: None known for non-residents; Ecobank Niger and Bank of Africa Niger serve residents.
Restrictions: Military government since 2023 and political isolation, BCEAO Instruction 09/07/2025/RFE tightened non-resident and FX account controls, correspondent-banking de-risking.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Mobile money (Airtel Money, Moov/Flooz) requires local SIM; foreigners rely on home accounts and remittance services.
Cost note: Non-residents cannot realistically open a personal account here, so no opening fee, minimum deposit or monthly fee applies or is published.

Documents required: Not applicable; historically only resident diplomats and aid workers could open foreign-currency accounts (e.g. Narae card).
Minimum deposit & fees: not published
Banks accepting non-residents: none known; Foreign Trade Bank and others are UN/US/Australian sanctioned.
Restrictions: Comprehensive UN, US and Australian autonomous sanctions; dealings with DPRK banks prohibited for Australians; no correspondent banking.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): none
Cost note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts here (all banks are under UN/US/Australian sanctions), so no costs apply.

Documents required: Passport, valid visa or proof of legal entry, migration card, Russian phone number; INN sometimes requested.
Minimum deposit & fees: Not published; MIR debit cards typically free to issue.
Banks accepting non-residents: T-Bank (formerly Tinkoff) issues accounts and MIR cards to any foreigner legally present; Sberbank and others case-by-case.
Restrictions: Australia is an unfriendly state: Central Bank restrictions on transfers abroad, Western sanctions on major banks (including Australian sanctions), no Visa/Mastercard international use; dealing may breach Australian sanctions law.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): None from abroad; Wise and Revolut do not support RUB transfers.
Cost note: T-Bank and other banks typically issue MIR debit cards and accounts free of charge (RUB about 80/USD), but the non-resident minimum balance and monthly fees could not be checked against a current tariff.

Documents required: Passport, Cabo Verdean tax number (NIF, issued at a Casa do Cidadao), local address and phone, signed opening form.
Minimum deposit & fees: Minimum opening deposit varies by bank; not published.
Banks accepting non-residents: Caixa Economica de Cabo Verde, BCA, Banco InterAtlantico, Ecobank.
Restrictions: Non-residents and tourists can open accounts but no standard fully remote route; cards collected at branch; escudo pegged to euro.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Wise EUR account for transfers.
Cost note: Caixa Economica, BCA, Banco InterAtlantico and Ecobank do not publish non-resident minimum deposits or maintenance fees retrievable this pass, so all figures are null.

Documents required: Passport, proof of address (lease or residential proof), purpose of account; branch presence required.
Minimum deposit & fees: Not published.
Banks accepting non-residents: ProCredit Bank Kosovo, Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, TEB Bank (case-by-case for foreign non-residents).
Restrictions: Banks expect a branch visit with proof of address; online opening aimed at Kosovo diaspora; euro is local currency; Serbian dinar banking curtailed since 2024.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Wise, Revolut, Paysera (EUR IBANs).
Cost note: Kosovo: not published by the banks named and no official tariff could be found, so all three figures are left null.

Documents required: Passport, proof of address, likely US SSN/ITIN or foreign TIN and local presence; requirements not published.

Restrictions: USD economy served by US banks subject to FATCA and US KYC rules; small local banking market.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Keep funds in an Australian bank or Wise; Palau digital residency ID does not confer bank access.

Documents required: Photo ID (passport accepted) showing name, address and an identity number such as a CPR number, or residence/employment documents as substitutes, under Danish AML rules.
Minimum deposit & fees: not published
Banks accepting non-residents: none known; Gronlandsbanken and Bankivik (BankNordik's former Greenland site now redirects there) target local residents and newcomers and publish no non-resident personal offering.
Restrictions: Danish krone and Danish FSA supervision; onboarding geared to CPR-registered residents, and accounts are blocked if ID requirements are not met; non-residents must contact banks case by case.
Alternatives (fintech / regional): Wise or Revolut for DKK; a Danish bank account where eligible.
Cost note: Non-residents cannot open personal accounts at Gronlandsbanken or Bankivik, which serve local residents only, so all three are null.
